title: Flow Control
summary: Shut a dam gate so the tank holds exactly the volume needed, using definite integrals, net flow, substitution and symmetric limits.
subject: mathematics
ncertRef: Section 7.8, Definite integral by the second fundamental theorem
concepts: Constant of integration and an initial value
Net area when the integrand changes sign
Even and odd integrands over symmetric limits
learningOutcome: The student can evaluate a definite integral from an antiderivative, count a negative part as negative, use substitution, and use symmetry to cancel the odd terms over limits −a to a.

levels.title: Fill the tank
levels.adds: Baseline: the integral of a power is F(t) = t^(n+1)/(n+1), and the volume is F(b) − F(0), plus what the tank already holds (Ex 7.8 Q1 to Q8; Example 25).
hints: Find an antiderivative F of the rate, term by term.
The volume that arrives is F(b) − F(0).
If the tank already holds water, add that to the integral.

levels.title: The drain
levels.adds: New: where the rate is negative the integral subtracts, so it gives net volume, not the total that flowed (Section 7.8; Ex 7.8 Q9 to Q14).
hints: Find where the rate crosses zero: before it the water drains.
The definite integral already counts that part as negative.
Take F(b) − F(0) and compare it with the volume needed.

levels.title: A hidden power
levels.adds: New: integration by substitution, with u = t² + c and u′ = 2t, then the definite integral (Ex 7.2 Q1 to Q10; Examples 5, 6, 26).
hints: Look for a function whose derivative is also in the rate.
Put u = t² + c, so du = 2t dt.
The new antiderivative is a power of u: take its value at b minus at 0.

levels.title: The canal
levels.adds: New: over −a to a, odd terms integrate to 0 and even terms to twice the integral from 0 to a (Ex 7.10 Q8 to Q14; Example 29).
hints: Split f into even terms (x², x⁴) and odd terms (x, x³).
The odd terms cancel between −h and h.
Double the integral of the even terms from 0 to h.

misconceptions: The integral is always the total area
A definite integral needs a constant of integration
A negative integral means a mistake
